Article Title: PM Modi hails youth for taking India to arenas once beyond reach
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi

NEW DELHI: From PV Sindhu 's racquet in Tokyo to a privately built rocket lifting off from Sriharikota, PM Narendra Modi Sunday used Mann Ki Baat to say young Indians were taking the country into arenas once considered beyond reach.In his monthly radio address, Modi singled out Sindhu's Japan Open triumph, the launch of Vikram-1, and India's performance at international science Olympiads as signs of a confident generation succeeding in sports, science and technology."Our youth have achieved remarkable feats in sports recently. PV Sindhu has become the first Indian to win the Japan Open title in badminton; the entire nation is proud of this achievement of hers," Modi said.Turning to space, he said Vikram-1, India's first privately developed orbital rocket, showed what young innovators could achieve when new doors were opened. Built by Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace, it placed six payloads in low-Earth orbit on July 18. "Keeping the interests of the youth in mind, we opened up the space sector to private enterprise, and today, the world is witnessing the results."He praised school students for winning 12 gold and seven silver medals across physics, chemistry, biology and mathematics Olympiads.Meanwhile, he lauded the youth as the energy behind the resolve of a developed India and said they will also be its biggest beneficiary as he held a virtual interaction with young participants of "Viksit Vibrant Village" programme. "When the youth directly connect with the country's challenges and their solutions, then the future will certainly be bright," he said.Speaking to youngsters who had visited border villages as part of a govt initiative, he said, "The more India's youth understand its border villages, the more easily they will know the country and connect with all its corners."
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi used Mann Ki Baat to say young Indians were taking the country into arenas once considered beyond reach. He singled out Sindhu's Japan Open triumph, the launch of Vikram-1, and India's performance at international science Olympiads.

Article Title: 'Wapis nahi aane dega': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's form triggers fresh debate over Sanju Samson's India return
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Sanju Samson

Selection battle ahead

NEW DELHI: Former India cricketer Irfan Pathan suggests that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s impressive performances could make it difficult for anyone, including Sanju Samson , to reclaim his place in India’s T20I side.The young batter continued his fine form with a composed 81-run innings in the third and final T20I against Zimbabwe on July 26, showing both maturity and power on a challenging Harare pitch.He played some eye-catching shots, including a straight drive off a yorker from Brad Evans and a massive 102-metre six against Sikandar Raza.Praising the youngster, Pathan wrote, “Jiski vhi jagah lega ye bachha use wapis nahi aane dega…How Special this Vaibhav Suryavanshi is??" (Whoever's place this kid takes, he won't let them come back. How special is this Vaibhav Suryavanshi?)His comments have added to the debate over whether Sooryavanshi has moved ahead of Samson in India’s T20 plans.Samson started as India’s first-choice opener during the Ireland T20Is but managed only low scores, leading to Sooryavanshi getting opportunities in the England series.Although the youngster couldn’t produce big knocks consistently in that series and Samson returned for the fifth T20I, neither change helped India avoid a whitewash.Samson was then left out of the Zimbabwe T20I series, while Sooryavanshi grabbed his chance with another impressive innings. With India’s next T20 assignment set to be the Asian Games, the competition for the opening spot between Samson and Sooryavanshi is expected to remain a major talking point.At the same time, Abhishek Sharma ’s place at the top has also come under scrutiny after a poor run of scores. The opener has managed just 2, 8, 1, 3, 16 and 10 in his last six T20I innings, raising fresh questions over India’s preferred opening combination.
Article Summary: Former India cricketer Irfan Pathan says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's performances could make it difficult for anyone, including Sanju Samson, to reclaim his place in India’s T20I side. The young batter continued his fine form with a composed 81-run innings in the third and final T 20I against Zimbabwe on July 26.

Article Title: NEET protest: Jantar Mantar walls wiped clean, but message stays on after Dharmendra Pradhan's exit
Article Text:
NDMC workers repaint walls and clean roads around Jantar Mantar following the conclusion of the protest

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top priority to prevent exam irregularities? Stronger security measures Better monitoring and transparency 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: On Sunday, Jantar Mantar and the lanes leading to it felt both different and familiar.It was a day after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union education minister following 36 days of protest over the NEET paper leak.Signs of the protest were everywhere, but so also was evidence that an overnight effort was made to remove the traces of it.The slogans that had covered the walls had been painted over.The lanes had been cleaned. The main section, with the stage area, was out of bounds. Police said “cleaning was in progress”.The main entry points to the site were blocked. Those determined to get in found another way, through an inner lane, off Janpath.But after entering the lane, they were stopped from accessing the main area.Still, people came in scattered groups.There were surprisingly many first-time visitors from outside Delhi.Several of them said they couldn’t come on weekdays but had planned this visit in advance because they wanted to be part of the protest. Alongside them were those who had been at the site since Day 1, who were returning, despite the restrictions.Some reminders of the previous day’s events, however, could not be painted over.A few students who had been injured in the police action were back. Nearby, a car with shattered windows stood.Among those who returned was Sahil, a student who arrived at the protest site with a plaster on one foot and a walker to help him move.Surrounded by his friends, he carefully made his way through the lane, stopping to rest, and determined not to turn back.The injury was fresh, but his decision to return seemed older than the pain.When asked about his broken leg, Sahil smiled and briefly looked towards his friends standing beside him.“This happened when we were trying to run for cover,” he said.Not everyone who arrived at Jantar Mantar had been part of the movement from the beginning. Some had travelled hundreds of kilometres just to stand at the site once.Aniruddh, a student preparing for competitive exams, came from Saharanpur and was visiting the protest site for the first time.“I was a little late, but I really wanted to come here. I booked my train ticket in advance because I knew I might not be able to come during the weekdays,” he said.For students like him, the protest had become a way of showing solidarity with thousands of others who were questioning the impact of the paper leak on their future.Zubair, who travelled from Bhopal, said, “It is one thing to watch everything on social media, but when I saw what was happening here, I couldn’t stay in Bhopal anymore.”The visitors on Sunday also included people who had made Jantar Mantar part of their daily routine. Fahmina had been coming to the protest from Day 1 along with her husband, who works in a parking space nearby.Travelling from Ghaziabad every day, she stood through the restrictions and even faced lathis during the clashes.“I also have kids. One is completing Class XII, the other is doing graduation. If we don’t raise our voices now, what will happen to their future? That’s my only concern,” she said.Expressing relief over Pradhan’s resignation, she added, “Pradhan is gone. But if the next one is also like Pradhan, we will raise our voice again. This is about the future of the entire country.”For some younger visitors, reaching Jantar Mantar meant keeping their plans hidden from their parents.Nitin and Amit, Class XI students from Dwarka, did not tell their parents they were coming to the protest site.“On weekdays, we couldn’t come. We had studies and our parents would not allow it. Today, we said we’re going nearby, took the metro and came here,” Nitin said, as the two watched groups chant slogans.Some people were even seen breaching the adjacent boundary of the Jantar Mantar heritage monument to enter the lane.Another group was focused on cleaning up the place. A group of strangers who had come from different parts of India found themselves picking up garbage bags together.They encouraged others to join them. “We didn’t know each other before this at all,” said Priya, before calling out: “Naare baad mein lagana, pehle safai karo (Shout slogans later, first come and clean the place).”The protest had also changed the surrounding streets. Ice cream sellers and golgappa vendors found a new spot where demand remained steady as visitors continued to arrive.Street shops reopened after many days. “We could not open our shops as this whole street was filled with protesters. It’s a relief finally,” said a shopkeeper.By afternoon, the scattered groups slowly became a crowd. The police started dispersing them.Meanwhile, workers with paint cans moved from one place to the other.For many who gathered there on Sunday, simply being present was a statement in itself, and they said they would return if the need arose.
Article Summary: The main entry points to Jantar Mantar were blocked on Sunday. The main section, with the stage area, was out of bounds. Police said “cleaning was in progress’ But people came in scattered groups, including first-time visitors from outside Delhi.

Article Title: Why was former Minnesota Vikings Pro Bowler Everson Griffen arrested? Everything to know about the gross misdemeanor charge
Article Text:
Why was former Vikings Pro Bowler Everson Griffen arrested?(Getty)

Everson Griffen says arrest had nothing to do with drinking



Former Minnesota Vikings star Everson Griffen is back in the headlines, but this time it has nothing to do with football. The four-time Pro Bowler was arrested in Minnesota after police said he drove a vehicle that did not meet the restrictions tied to his driver's license.While the arrest raised fresh questions because of his past legal issues, authorities have not accused Griffen of driving under the influence in this case.According to a criminal complaint filed in Winona County, police stopped Everson Griffen at around 8 p.m. on July 23 after allegedly clocking his vehicle at 62 mph in a 40 mph zone on Riverview Drive in Winona, Minnesota. During the traffic stop, officers discovered that Griffen was driving a vehicle that allegedly did not have the ignition interlock device required under the terms of his restricted driver's license.An ignition interlock device requires a driver to provide a clean breath sample before a vehicle can start. Court records show Everson Griffen's driving privileges remain subject to that condition. Because the vehicle did not have the required system installed, officers arrested him on suspicion of violating his license restrictions. Prosecutors later charged him with a gross misdemeanor.He was released after posting bond and is scheduled to appear remotely in Winona County District Court on August 28.Soon after news of the arrest became public, Everson Griffen responded through a post on his Instagram account. He insisted the situation was an administrative issue and not a relapse."Nothing happened when I got pulled over last night. My license was revoked because I forgot to complete the required class/test, and I just moved, so I was planning to take care of both the class and the address change on Monday. I wasn't drinking, wasn't smoking, and wasn't doing anything wrong. Everything is fine."Everson Griffen shared that statement on Instagram shortly after his arrest. The criminal complaint adds another detail.According to court documents, an officer asked Griffen whether the required ignition interlock system was installed in the vehicle. The complaint says Griffen replied that he had taken the test to regain his license but failed it. A supervising officer then checked state records and confirmed that his license still carried the ignition interlock restriction.That point matters because the current case does not accuse Griffen of driving while impaired. Instead, it focuses on whether he violated the conditions attached to his restricted license. The arrest comes after a difficult stretch away from football. Griffen has spoken openly in recent months about rebuilding his life and recently said he was approaching one year of sobriety. He has also faced previous driving-related legal issues, including an impaired-driving conviction that led to the license restrictions. Local reports also said he received a citation in August 2025 after allegedly driving 130 mph in a 60 mph zone.Despite those off-field struggles, Griffen remains one of the most accomplished defensive players in Minnesota Vikings history. The Vikings selected him in the fourth round of the 2010 NFL Draft, and he spent 11 of his 12 NFL seasons with the franchise. He earned four Pro Bowl selections and finished his career with 88.5 sacks, including 85.5 with Minnesota.Now, the focus shifts to the courtroom. Griffen's Aug. 28 hearing will determine the next step in the case, while the former Vikings star continues to maintain that his arrest should not be mistaken for another alcohol-related incident.
Article Summary: Everson Griffen was arrested after police said he drove a vehicle that did not meet the restrictions tied to his driver's license. Authorities have not accused Griffen of driving under the influence in this case. He has also faced previous driving-related legal issues, including an impaired-driving conviction that led to the license restrictions.

Article Title: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation
Article Text:
The name 'Anahat' came from Guru Nanak's prayer

Aad aneel anaad anaahat jug jug ayko vays

Anahat stays true to its meaning

READ ALSO:

NEW DELHI:. This exact line appears once at the close of four consecutive stanzas, Pauris 28, 29, 30, and 31, of Japji Sahib, composed by Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, in the opening composition of the Guru Granth Sahib.Translated, it reads roughly as: The One is primal, stainless, without beginning, self-existent (unstruck), and the same throughout all ages.Japji Sahib opens the Guru Granth Sahib, Sikhism's central scripture, and it's the prayer devout Sikhs recite every morning as part of their daily practice. Tucked inside that refrain is the word anaahat, which means unstruck, unbeaten, a sound that exists without ever being produced by collision. It is also, as it happens, the name of one of Indian sport's most exciting young athletes, Anahat Singh."My husband came up with it," Anahat's mother, Tani Vadera Singh, had earlier told TimesofIndia.com . "He was reading the Sikh prayer, Japji Sahib. And in the last line, there is, he knows it, the name Anahat."On March 13, 2008, Gursharan Singh was reading the prayer in the hospital room the day his daughter was born. Something about the word stopped him."He said, you know, this sounds really nice," Tani recalled."I would like to name her that. So that is how (Anahat was named)."There was no grand plan behind it, and there wasn't one behind her sporting career either, at least not at first.The Singh-Vadera household was simply a sporting one. Tani played hockey for Delhi at the sub-junior and junior levels; Gursharan played hockey at St. Stephen's College and had hoped to play for India before academics took over. Uncle Deepak Vadera was once one of India's finest table tennis players. Anahat's elder sister, Amira, played tennis before switching to squash, and Anahat herself started on badminton at six, following the family's simple house rule that sport mattered as much as school."We always feel that sport is as important as studies," Tani admitted.Anahat trailed her sister into squash next, and the family openly admits they had no idea what they were building. "We didn't obviously imagine all this happening," Tani added. "We were just playing for fun."Father Gursharan, who'd never played the sport himself, taught himself squash so he could help train her, working alongside her coaches. It stayed lighthearted for years, Anahat wanting, as a five-year-old, to be an Olympic champion, though she was picturing badminton at the time, not the sport she'd eventually take to a world stage.The turn toward seriousness came once she made the Commonwealth Games squad at 13, a milestone her mother pinpoints as the moment "fun" started sharing space with real expectation.That balance of joy and intensity has produced a résumé most players twice her age would envy.Anahat debuted for India at 14 at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, won Asian Games medals at 16, and climbed inside the world's top 20 as she transitioned onto the senior circuit.On Saturday, the 18-year-old added the achievement that may end up defining her junior career, having become the first Indian ever to win the World Junior Squash Championship, beating Egypt's Ruqayya Salem 3-0 in the final in Niagara-on-the-Lake, Canada, without dropping a single game across the whole tournament.She'd beaten two other Egyptian players en route, a country that had held this exact title for sixteen consecutive years running. The last non-Egyptian to win it at all was American Amanda Sobhy, back in 2010.It's a fitting full circle. A name lifted from Guru Nanak's prayer has travelled from the rhythm of a morning recitation to the biggest stage in junior squash. Anahat Singh gave it a new association of her own by living up to the poise and permanence it has come to represent.
Article Summary: Anahat Singh is the first Indian ever to win the World Junior Squash Championship. The 18-year-old's name comes from the prayer Japji Sahib, Sikhism's central scripture. Anahat's father, Gursharan, was reading the prayer in the hospital room the day she was born.

Article Text:

India enjoyed its most successful day so far at the 2026 Commonwealth Games on Sunday, collecting one gold and two silver medals to take its overall tally to four medals, while boxers continued their impressive run and the men's swimming relay team reached another Commonwealth final.Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu headlined India's Day 4 performances by winning her third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal, while Rishikanta Singh and Raja Muthupandi added silver medals in weightlifting. Elsewhere, Jadumani Singh booked his place in the boxing quarter-finals with a commanding victory over Pakistan's Sumama Rehman, Preeti Pawar advanced with a stoppage win, and the men's 4x200m freestyle relay team qualified for and competed in the final.Saikhom Mirabai Chanu once again underlined her status as one of India's greatest weightlifters by winning the women's 48kg gold medal.The Tokyo Olympic silver medallist overcame an unsuccessful opening attempt before producing another dominant performance, finishing with a combined lift of 190kg. She set a new Commonwealth Games record of 85kg in the snatch before lifting 105kg in the clean and jerk to comfortably secure the title.The victory completed a remarkable hat-trick of Commonwealth Games gold medals after her triumphs in Gold Coast in 2018 and Birmingham in 2022. It also took her overall Commonwealth Games medal tally to four.Rishikanta Singh Chanambam delivered an outstanding performance to secure silver in the men's 60kg event.The 28-year-old lifter from Manipur successfully cleared 116kg, 119kg and 121kg in the snatch, with his best effort equalling the Commonwealth Games record.He then managed 143kg in the clean and jerk but narrowly missed attempts at 148kg and 151kg, finishing with a total lift of 264kg.Malaysia's Muhammad Anik bin Kasdan won gold with a Games-record total of 273kg, while Kenya's Joshua Amunga Buoya claimed bronze after lifting 260kg.Raja Muthupandi ensured India finished the day with three weightlifting medals by taking silver in the men's 65kg category.The Tamil Nadu lifter recorded 126kg in the snatch before adding 160kg in the clean and jerk to finish with a combined total of 286kg.Malaysia's Muhamad Aznil Bin Bidin captured gold after setting a Commonwealth Games record total of 299kg, while Papua New Guinea's Morea Baru secured bronze with 282kg.The silver capped a remarkable comeback for Muthupandi, who returned to the Commonwealth Games podium eight years after finishing sixth on his debut at Gold Coast in 2018 following an injury-disrupted spell that also saw him miss Birmingham 2022.India enjoyed another productive day inside the boxing ring.Jadumani Singh Mandengbam defeated Pakistan's Sumama Rehman by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the men's 55kg Round of 16 to book his place in the quarter-finals.After a closely contested opening round, the Manipur boxer gradually took control of the contest, scoring a knockdown in the second round before sealing victory on all five judges' scorecards. He will next face England's Ellis Trowbridge for a place in the medal rounds.In the women's 54kg Round of 16, Preeti Pawar produced a dominant display to defeat Malawi's Deborah Mtenje by referee stops contest (RSC), advancing comfortably to the quarter-finals.India also suffered one boxing setback as Aditya Pratap Yadav narrowly lost to Uganda's Nuhu Batte in the men's 65kg Round of 16 by a 3-2 split decision.India's men's 4x200m freestyle relay quartet of Srihari Nataraj, Aryan Nehra, Aneesh Gowda and Dhakshan Shashikumar successfully qualified for the final after finishing third in Heat 2.The Indian team clocked 7:39.48 to finish behind Australia and England while holding off Jersey to secure progression. They advanced as the sixth-fastest team overall from the combined heats.Later in the evening, the same quartet returned for the medal race and finished sixth in the Commonwealth Games final.India endured a difficult day in lawn bowls.Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki Singh first lost 3-0 to Namibia in a women's pairs sectional play tiebreak before suffering another defeat against England, ending their campaign in the event.In the men's singles, Putul Sonowal lost his sectional play match against Malta's Shaun James Parnis.Artistic gymnast Tapan Mohanty finished 15th in the men's all-around final.India's women's 3x3 wheelchair basketball team also suffered defeat, losing 21-4 to Scotland in Pool B.India concluded Day 4 with four medals overall at the Games; one gold, two silvers and one bronze, with the boxing contingent continuing to build momentum heading into the quarter-final stage.
Article Summary: India enjoyed its most successful day so far at the 2026 Commonwealth Games on Sunday, collecting one gold and two silver medals. Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu won her third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal. Rishikanta Singh and Raja Muthupandi added silver medals in weightlifting. Jadumani Singh booked his place in the boxing quarter-finals with a commanding victory over Pakistan's Sumama Rehman. The men's 4x200m freestyle relay team qualified for and competed in the final.

Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripts history, creates world record at just 15
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (ANI Photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view What impressed you the most about Sooryavanshi's performance in Zimbabwe? His ability to adapt to different pitches. His consistency across matches. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi added another milestone to his remarkable start in international cricket after becoming the youngest player to win a Player of the Series award in men's international cricket.The 15-year-old achieved the feat after starring in India's 3-0 T20I series sweep over Zimbabwe in Harare. Sooryavanshi finished as the leading run-scorer of the series with 151 runs in three innings and capped off the campaign with a match-winning 81 off 49 balls in the final T20I.The left-handed opener showed impressive adaptability throughout the series. After announcing himself with a blistering 50 off just 18 balls in the opening match, Sooryavanshi produced a more measured innings in the decider on a sluggish pitch. His knock of 81, laced with eight fours and four sixes, powered India to 192/5 before the visitors completed a 35-run victory.His consistency across the three matches earned him the Player of the Series award, making him the youngest recipient of the honour in men's international cricket.Speaking after receiving the award, Sooryavanshi credited his preparation for the successful series."I try to replicate what I do in training," he said. "I had good preparation time after the England tour and I am glad to score these runs for the team, and contribute to the series win.It was my dream to do it for India."The award marked a significant turnaround for the teenager, who had endured a difficult maiden international series in England earlier this month. After replacing Sachin Tendulkar as India's youngest men's international cricketer, Sooryavanshi managed scores of 14, 13 and 15 in the T20I series against England before being left out of the final game, which India also lost to concede the series 4-0.However, the selectors persisted with the young batter for the Zimbabwe tour, backing him to rediscover the form that had made him one of India's brightest prospects. Their faith was rewarded as Sooryavanshi dominated at the Harare Sports Club, a venue where he had already made headlines earlier this year with a stunning 175 off 80 balls against England in the Under-19 World Cup final.His latest achievement further underlined his rapid rise, with the teenager not only playing a decisive role in India's series victory but also entering the record books as the youngest-ever Player of the Series winner in men's international cricket.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is youngest ever Player of the Series winner in men's international cricket. The 15-year-old scored 151 runs in three innings in India's 3-0 T20I series sweep over Zimbabwe. He capped off the campaign with a match-winning 81 off 49 balls in the final match.

Article Title: FIFA President Gianni Infantino travelled almost three times the Earth's circumference during the World Cup
Article Text:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino attends the World Cup Group D soccer match between the United States and Paraguay in Inglewood, Calif., near Los Angeles, Friday, June 12, 2026. (AP Photo/Andre Penner)

Flight data highlights environmental impact

FIFA president Gianni Infantino signs autographs after Spain defeated France the World Cup semifinal soccer match in Arlington, Texas, near Dallas, Tuesday, July 14, 2026. (AP Photo/Eric Gay)

Expanded tournament increases travel demands

FIFA President Gianni Infantino, centre, stands with United States Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, left, and Director of the FBI, Kash Patel ahead of the World Cup Group K soccer match between Colombia and Portugal in Miami Gardens, Fla., Saturday, June 27, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)

Campaign groups question consistency

President Donald Trump, left, and FIFA President Gianni Infantino attend the World Cup championship final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

FIFA defends president's travel

FIFA president Gianni Infantino's travel during the 2026 World Cup has come under renewed scrutiny after reports detailed the extent of his use of private air travel throughout the tournament, prompting criticism from climate campaigners who questioned whether it aligned with FIFA's own environmental commitments.According to reports, Infantino attended 44 of the tournament's 104 matches between the opening game on June 11 and the final between Spain and Argentina on July 19. The expanded tournament was staged across 16 host cities in the United States, Canada and Mexico, making it the largest and geographically widest World Cup in history.Infantino visited every host city during the competition, frequently attending more than one match per day.On several occasions during the group stage, he watched two matches in different cities, while some days reportedly involved three separate flights to accommodate his schedule.The extensive travel has attracted attention because of the environmental impact associated with private aviation, particularly as FIFA has repeatedly pledged to reduce its carbon footprint.According to the Mirror's analysis of flight data, Infantino travelled approximately 106,323 kilometres (66,066 miles) during the tournament aboard a Gulfstream G650 private jet, producing an estimated 1,020.3 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e).This distance is roughly equivalent to circling the Earth almost three times, based on the planet’s circumference of about 40,075 kilometres.The BBC noted that the Gulfstream G650ER, the aircraft believed to have been used during the tournament, has an average fuel consumption of approximately 1,817 litres per hour. Using the UK government's greenhouse gas conversion methodology, the broadcaster estimated the emissions produced during the group phase.Infantino has previously been photographed travelling aboard Qatar Airways Executive aircraft, while reports during this World Cup indicated he was again using a Gulfstream G650ER.The 2026 edition marked the first World Cup featuring 48 teams and was jointly hosted by three countries, significantly increasing travel requirements for teams, officials, media and supporters.According to FIFA's own environmental assessments, the tournament was projected to generate approximately nine million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions, almost double the average recorded across World Cups staged between 2010 and 2022. Air travel represents the largest contributor to those emissions.Despite those figures, FIFA has committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 50 per cent by 2030 and achieving net-zero emissions by 2040.Ahead of the tournament, the governing body outlined several sustainability initiatives, including regionalising team accommodation to reduce long-haul travel where possible, promoting electric vehicles and public transport, improving energy efficiency and encouraging water conservation.The issue of FIFA's environmental claims has previously attracted regulatory attention. In 2023, a Swiss regulator concluded that FIFA had made false statements by describing the 2022 Qatar World Cup as the first carbon-neutral tournament, after relying on carbon-offsetting measures. Following that ruling, FIFA said it recognised climate change as "one of the most pressing challenges of our time" and believed immediate, sustainable action was necessary.Several environmental organisations argued that Infantino's travel choices undermined FIFA's sustainability messaging.Frank Huisingh, founder of Fossil Free Football, said the private jet travel contrasted sharply with the conditions experienced by players and supporters during the tournament."As players and supporters struggled through extreme heat, Infantino's Qatari private jet took him from VIP box to VIP box across his bloated tournament," Huisingh said."There could be no more perfect illustration for FIFA's wilful blindness to the climate threats facing football and its fans."Katie Cross, chief executive of sports sustainability charity Pledgeball, said the reported emissions reflected "a complete disregard for the longevity of the game, the players and the fans who make it."Andrew Simms, director of the New Weather Institute, described the aircraft's emissions as leaving behind "a cloud of contempt", while Freddie Daley of the Cool Down Sport for Climate Action Network told BBC Sport that the apparent reliance on private aviation was "symptomatic of FIFA's failings on the environment and sustainability."Jenny Amann, a doctoral researcher at Loughborough University who studies supporters' attitudes towards climate change and football, said interviews with fans consistently revealed criticism of FIFA's leadership on environmental issues.She argued that Infantino's reported travel emissions were "hundreds of times greater than the average European football fan produces in an entire year", adding that such actions were unlikely to encourage supporters to adopt more sustainable behaviours.FIFA has defended the president's travel arrangements, maintaining that his schedule reflected official duties across a tournament spread over an entire continent.A FIFA spokesperson told BBC Sport that the president "routinely travels, together with relevant officials, on business and tournament-related matters and strives to visit member associations of FIFA whenever he can."The spokesperson added that travel arrangements are made according to operational requirements."Sometimes travel is organised on commercial, including low-cost—airlines and sometimes it is on private charter, depending on which is more efficient and cost-effective under the circumstances."The governing body also stated that FIFA has established internal rules governing travel by its officials.Unlike the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, where Infantino attended all 64 matches across eight stadiums located within relatively short travelling distance of one another, the 2026 tournament presented far greater logistical challenges because of its expanded format and the vast distances separating host cities across North America.While the scale of Infantino's travel has prompted renewed debate over football's environmental impact, FIFA maintains that its long-term sustainability commitments remain unchanged as it continues pursuing its targets of halving emissions by 2030 and reaching net-zero by 2040.
Article Summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino's travel during the 2026 World Cup has come under renewed scrutiny. Reports detailed the extent of his use of private air travel throughout the tournament. FIFA has committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 50 per cent by 2030 and achieving net-zero emissions by 2040. The 2026 edition marked the first World Cup featuring 48 teams.

Article Title: 'Dedicate my win to Kargil heroes': Indian boxer Jadumani Singh Mandengbam after beating Pakistan's Sumama Rehman at CWG 2026
Article Text:
India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam (PTI Photo/Ravi Choudhary)

Indian boxer Jadumani Singh Mandengbam moved into the men's 55kg quarterfinals at the Commonwealth Games 2026 after defeating Pakistan's Sumama Rehman by a unanimous 5-0 decision on Sunday.The convincing victory came on Kargil Vijay Diwas , making the win even more special for the 22-year-old, who dedicated it to India's Kargil War heroes.After the bout, Jadumani said, "I dedicate my win to the Kargil heroes. I felt great winning against Pakistan. I will perform even better in the quaterfinals and secure a Gold for India."His victory coincided with the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas, when India honoured the soldiers who sacrificed their lives during the 1999 Kargil War. Jadumani stayed in control throughout the contest against Rehman, earning all five judges' votes to seal a comfortable win.The Manipuri boxer had already impressed in the opening round with another 5-0 win over Scotland's Aaron Cullen. His latest victory takes him into the last eight, where he will fight on Tuesday for a place in the semifinals.A win in the quarterfinal will also guarantee him at least a bronze medal, as both losing semifinalists in Commonwealth Games boxing receive bronze.Jadumani, who won silver in the 50kg category at last year's World Boxing Cup Finals before moving up to the 55kg division, has looked in excellent form with back-to-back unanimous victories.India also enjoyed success in other events on Sunday, with Mirabai Chanu winning her third straight Commonwealth Games gold in weightlifting, while Chanambam Rishikanta Singh and Raja Muthupandi claimed silver medals, adding to the country's strong medal haul in Glasgow.

Stefon Diggs remains a free agent with training camps already underway, but the wait may finally be ending. After a legal cloud that lingered over his market cleared last month, fresh reporting from ESPN's Jeremy Fowler now points to one team pulling ahead of the pack: the Washington Commanders. Here's everything currently known about where the four-time Pro Bowler could land.Washington has emerged as the clear favorite. According to Fowler, the Commanders still need a true complement to Terry McLaurin, and word around the league is that a receiver addition "should shake out" for Diggs sooner rather than later. Diggs also has local ties as a Maryland native, adding a hometown angle to the fit.Washington had been floated as a landing spot for Brandon Aiyuk earlier in the offseason, but his recent combative social media activity has reportedly given the front office cold feet, clearing a path for Diggs instead.The Baltimore Ravens have also been mentioned as a fallback suitor, given questions about their receiver depth behind Zay Flowers, though Washington remains the far more active conversation right now.Diggs' free agency stalled for months partly because teams were waiting on the outcome of an NFL personal conduct investigation tied to an alleged incident involving his former chef. That cleared up in June when the league announced there was insufficient evidence to support a violation, removing a major hurdle for suitors who'd been sitting on the sidelines.Fowler also notes a key difference from last year: Diggs enters this market fully healthy, not rehabbing the torn ACL that limited him during his lone Patriots season. Despite that, he still played roughly 55% of New England's offensive snaps and cleared 1,000 yards, a track record that's kept his market alive even at 32.Diggs is coming off a one-year "prove it" deal with the Patriots that was structured to let both sides evaluate fit. New England released him in March, citing his cap number and the pending legal matter, both of which have since resolved in his favor as he heads into a fresh market. No specific asking price has been reported yet, but as an outright free agent (not a trade candidate), any signing would come with no compensation owed to New England.Terry McLaurin would remain Washington's clear WR1, continuing to draw top coverage weekly. Still, Diggs' presence would give young quarterback Jayden Daniels a proven, savvy second option to attack softer looks underneath and in the slot. For a Commanders team that reached the divisional round with Super Bowl aspirations before slipping to a top-10 pick, adding a veteran of Diggs' caliber even at this stage of his career gives their receiver room real juice heading into the season.Nothing is finalized, and no contract has been reported yet. But with camps open, Diggs healthy, and his legal situation behind him, a decision looks close, and right now, all signs point to Washington.As training camp gets going, Stefon Diggs is still waiting for the right opportunity. The Commanders may be a strong possibility, but no deal has been made yet. For now, the veteran wide receiver is taking his time, and his next move is expected to be one of the biggest stories to watch before the regular season begins.
Article Summary: Stefon Diggs' free agency mystery just got a very specific answer. Diggs is "highly motivated" toward Washington Commanders, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Washington had been floated as a landing spot for Brandon Aiyuk earlier in the offseason. Baltimore Ravens have also been mentioned as a fallback suitor.

Article Title: 'Why different rules for different players?' - Abhishek Sharma's poor form sparks Sanju Samson debate
Article Text:
India's Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson (ANI Photo)

Hanuma Vihari has questioned Team India's decision to continue backing Abhishek Sharma despite his poor run of form in the ongoing T20I series against Zimbabwe. The former India batter believes the selectors have applied different standards to Abhishek and Sanju Samson, especially after Samson lost his place despite performing well in major tournaments.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Vihari pointed out that Samson was dropped after a few poor games before the T20 World Cup but returned strongly to become one of India's standout performers.He said, "Before the World Cup, Sanju Samson did not perform in five games and lost his spot in the starting 11. He then made a comeback and became Player of the Tournament. In that same tournament, how many runs did Abhishek Sharma make?"He also highlighted Abhishek's recent numbers, saying, "In the UK series, apart from one fifty, there were no scores at all. Not even 20s and 30s, no significant score. One fifty in the last eight matches. If you include the World Cup, three half-centuries in the last 18 matches."Vihari argued that Samson proved himself when it mattered by scoring three consecutive fifties during India's T20 World Cup-winning campaign, but still lost his place in the side as youngster Vaibhav Sooryavanshi emerged as a preferred option.Questioning the selection policy, he said, "How many matches Samson played in the World Cup? Three. And fifties in all three. Abhishek's highest score in the five matches is 16. Why is no one talking about it? When it comes to Samson, they say he is inconsistent. Fair enough. But he can win high-pressure matches on his day."Vihari concluded by adding, "Abhishek is a player with a lot of hype, but Samson is also equal. He has also performed in the IPL. Why different rules for different players?"

Article Title: Did Lionel Messi really give every Argentina player a gold Stanley set after losing the World Cup? Here’s the truth behind the viral gift
Article Text:
Kelci-Rose Bowers showed the personalized mate collection Lionel Messi gave Marcos Senesi after Argentina’s 2026 World Cup campaign. (Image via Getty)

Lionel Messi gave Argentina players personalized mate sets after the World Cup

The gift followed Argentina’s painful loss to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final

Lionel Messi left the 2026 World Cup without another title, but his Argentina teammates did not leave empty-handed.Kelci-Rose Bowers, the partner of Argentina defender Marcos Senesi, revealed that Messi gave every member of Lionel Scaloni’s squad a personalized mate set after the tournament. The collection included a custom bag, a gold-colored Stanley thermos, a mate cup, a metal straw and yerba mate. Multiple sources have reported details from Bowers’ social media video. So, yes, Messi did give every Argentina teammate a personalized Stanley set after the 2026 World Cup, but the bottles were gold-colored, not made of gold.Bowers showed Senesi’s gift in a video after Argentina’s campaign ended. The caramel-colored bag carried Senesi’s name, the Argentina crest, the World Cup logo and light blue details.“This is a personalised bag that Marcos got from the camp,” Bowers said. Inside the bag was a gold-colored Stanley thermos marked with Messi’s logo. The set also contained a mate cup, a bombilla straw and yerba mate, the dried leaves used to prepare the drink. Bowers said Messi gave the same type of set to every player in Argentina’s squad.“I have to show you guys something really cool. You will be very happy to see this. Marcos brought this bag from the camp.It also has his name written on it. This is his mate set. Messi gave this gift to all the players,” she said.Senesi then left the collection with Bowers for safekeeping. “Marcos gave me it to keep safe and take back to Miami,” she said.Bowers later described it as a “pretty cool gift” and said it was “pretty cool that I’ve got it.”The gift was personal because mate is part of Argentina’s daily team culture. Players regularly carry mate sets to training, hotels and stadiums. They prepare and share the drink together, so Messi selected something tied directly to the squad’s routine rather than a generic luxury item.The choice also matched Messi’s history of giving personalized gifts to Argentina teammates. After the 2022 World Cup, he reportedly commissioned 35 gold iPhones for players and staff. Reports at the time valued that collection at more than $200,000.Messi handed out the sets after Argentina fell short of winning consecutive World Cups. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final on July 19 at New York New Jersey Stadium. Ferran Torres scored the deciding goal in the 106th minute.Argentina had entered the final with a chance to become the first country since Brazil in 1962 to defend the World Cup. Messi could not score or assist in the loss, ending his run of 11 straight World Cup appearances with a goal contribution.Even so, the 39-year-old finished the tournament with eight goals and four assists in eight matches. Argentina reached another final four years after winning in Qatar, but Spain ended the repeat bid.Senesi joined Argentina’s squad late after Leonardo Balerdi suffered an injury. He made his World Cup debut in a 3-1 group-stage win over Jordan and later appeared again during the knockout rounds.The mate set now links Senesi’s first World Cup to Messi’s final act as captain during the tournament. It also showed how Messi responded after the defeat. He did not blame teammates or distance himself from the group. He gave every player the same personalized collection built around a shared Argentina tradition.Messi’s international future remained uncertain after the final, but the gift offered one clear message. The World Cup ended in disappointment. The squad still left with a reminder of the group that reached the final together.
Article Summary: Lionel Messi gave Argentina players personalized mate sets after the World Cup. The gift followed Argentina's painful loss to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. The collection included a custom bag, a gold-colored Stanley thermos, a mate cup, a metal straw and yerba mate.

Article Title: What the latest Baker Mayfield report really says about Tampa Bay's confidence in its $47 million franchise quarterback
Article Text:
Baker Mayfield (Getty Images)

Could the Buccaneers use the franchise tag instead of giving Baker Mayfield a new contract?

Baker Mayfield's contract situation in Tampa Bay is getting messier and more fascinating by the week. The Buccaneers quarterback is in the final year of a reworked deal worth $27 million in 2026, with no long-term extension anywhere close to the horizon. And now, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the franchise tag is emerging as a very real possibility for 2027 -- one that could cost Tampa Bay at least $47 million.A franchise tag has rarely been part of the public discussion around Mayfield's future, but Fowler believes it remains a realistic possibility."While Mayfield would prefer a long-term deal, he’s not afraid of the franchise tag, which would cost Tampa Bay at least $47M in 2027," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler wrote on his official X account on Sunday.From Mayfield's perspective, the financial risk appears limited. He has already earned significant money during his NFL career and is due another $40 million this season. That gives him room to be patient rather than force negotiations."Baker has made $131.8 million already in his career & he’ll make $40 million this season," Damage Inc. wrote on X on Sunday. "Getting tagged at $47 million at age 32 won’t faze him at all.I’m sure he would like another nine-digit contract, but he’s going to make over $200 million in his career regardless."While the financial side remains stable, Mayfield enters the season with something else to prove. Last year started in impressive fashion as both he and the Buccaneers looked like one of the NFL's biggest success stories through the first six weeks. That momentum faded quickly. Tampa Bay finished 8-9, missed the playoffs for the first time since 2019 and Mayfield's standing across the league took a hit.ESPN's annual survey of NFL executives, coaches and scouts reflected that shift. After previously being viewed among the league's top quarterbacks, Mayfield dropped out of the Top 10 and landed in the honourable mention category. He also missed out on the Pro Bowl after earning selections in each of his first two seasons with Tampa Bay.Even so, respect for his game has not disappeared. Mayfield was the only quarterback from the NFC South to receive votes in the rankings."Mayfield is a winner," one anonymous NFL coordinator told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. "He can make every throw. Fearless. Article Title: Why was Isaiah Rider arrested? Former Lakers star is in police custody in a case related to his wife Vanessa

What happened to Isaiah Rider?

Is Isaiah Rider's latest arrest related to his wife Vanessa?

Isaiah Rider was arrested again Thursday night, his third arrest in less than two months, this time on a misdemeanor charge for failing to comply with a court order. Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible. They give me peace of mind” - How Rafael Nadal’s fam

How did Rafael Nadal overcome a career-threatening foot condition?

Why did Rafael Nadal always choose family and home over fame?

What did Rafael Nadal say about his wife and family during his injury battles?

What life lesson did Rafael Nadal learn from pain and defeat?

For years, Rafael Nadal inspired fans with his fight on the tennis court. What many people did not see was the battle he fought away from the spotlight. Long before becoming a 22-time Grand Slam champion, Nadal was told that a rare foot condition could end his career. He dealt with constant pain, serious injuries and doubts about whether he could keep playing. Yet he kept coming back. While his determination made headlines, Nadal has always said his biggest strength was the people who stood beside him. Their support helped him survive the hardest moments and build one of the greatest careers in tennis history.In 2005, Nadal won his first French Open title at just 19 years old. Soon after that breakthrough, he was diagnosed with Mueller-Weiss syndrome, a rare condition that affects the bones in the foot.Doctors warned that continuing his career at the highest level might not be possible.Instead of giving up, Nadal returned home to Manacor in Mallorca. There, he was surrounded by his father Sebastián, mother Ana María, sister Maribel and his longtime partner Mery Perelló. Their support gave him the strength to keep moving forward when his future looked uncertain.Looking back on those difficult years, Nadal once said:“Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible.They give me peace of mind.”Despite becoming one of the biggest names in world sport, Nadal never left the place where he grew up. He stayed close to his family in Manacor and continued living the simple life that had shaped him from childhood.His uncle and longtime coach Toni Nadal taught him to stay humble, respect opponents and never believe he was bigger than the game. Those lessons stayed with him throughout his career.Nadal has often explained that returning home helped him switch off from the pressure of professional tennis. In Manacor, he was simply Rafa, spending time with friends and family. That normal life became an important part of maintaining his mental balance through the highs and lows of the sport.Nadal’s wife, Mery “Xisca” Perelló, was by his side long before he became a global star. She witnessed every comeback, every rehabilitation session and every painful setback that fans rarely saw.As injuries continued in the final years of his career, those shared sacrifices became even more meaningful. With his wife, young son and team watching from the stands, Nadal reflected on everything they had gone through together.He said:“Having my family here, my wife, my son, my team… it’s emotional because they know how hard the process has been. They have been through the good moments, but especially the tough moments during all these years of injuries.”Nadal never believed success came without suffering. Throughout his career, he played through injuries, long matches and physical pain that would have stopped many athletes. Instead of running from those challenges, he accepted them as part of the journey.That mindset became one of the biggest reasons behind his remarkable career.As Nadal explained:“If you don’t lose, you cannot enjoy the victories. You have to accept both things. I learned during my career to enjoy suffering.”His story goes far beyond Grand Slam trophies or records. It shows that true strength is not only about winning titles but also about staying grounded when life becomes difficult. Through every injury and every comeback, Nadal never lost sight of the people who mattered most. Their love gave him the peace, confidence and support to keep chasing his dreams, making his journey one of the most inspiring stories in modern sport.
Article Summary: Rafael Nadal was diagnosed with a career-threatening foot condition in 2005. Doctors told him it could end his career, but he refused to give up. Instead of giving up, Nadal returned home to Manacor in Mallorca. There, he was surrounded by his father, mother and sister. Their support gave him the strength to keep moving forward when his future looked uncertain.
