Article Title: North Carolina spent 25 years rebuilding an elk population that had disappeared from the state; in 2027, it will allow its first limited hunt with just two permits
Article Text:
Elk were once found across much of North Carolina but disappeared from the state many years ago

The hunt

Elk in western North Carolina. (Photos: WLOS)

The permits

The rules

For the first time since elk were reintroduced to western North Carolina 25 years ago, the state will allow a limited elk hunting season. The decision comes after wildlife officials said the elk population has recovered enough to support controlled hunting while continuing conservation efforts.The change follows the signing of House Bill 747 by North Carolina Governor Josh Stein on July 7. The law allows the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission (NCWRC) to issue two elk hunting permits during the 2027 hunting season.Officials say the move is not aimed at reducing the population quickly but is part of a long-term wildlife management plan. The money raised through the permits will also be used for elk conservation and management.Elk were once found across much of North Carolina but disappeared from the state many years ago because of overhunting and habitat loss. Wildlife agencies later began efforts to bring them back to western North Carolina, and the animals have slowly established a stable population over the past 25 years.According to Justin McVey, district wildlife biologist with the NCWRC, the state has now reached an important milestone."Our goal for elk management in the state is to have a sustainable huntable population and at this point we've reached that goal," McVey said, as quoted by ABC 13 news.A sustainable population means there are enough animals to maintain healthy numbers while also allowing a limited number to be hunted without affecting the long-term survival of the species.The state is taking a cautious approach by issuing only two permits during the first hunting season. The two permits will be distributed in different ways.One permit will be auctioned through a wildlife conservation non-profit organisation that took part in the elk reintroduction programme in North Carolina.Under the law, the selected non-profit can keep up to 25% of the auction proceeds. The remaining money will go towards wildlife conservation.The second permit will be issued through a public raffle. Raffle tickets will cost $20 each, and participants can buy up to 30 tickets for $500. To enter, buyers must have a valid North Carolina hunting licence or be eligible for a licence exemption under state regulations.The Wildlife Resources Commission may receive up to $25,000 from the raffle proceeds. The rest of the money collected from both the auction and raffle will be deposited into the state's Wildlife Resources Fund, where it will be used for elk conservation and management programmes.McVey said the permits are expected to become available in July 2027. The elk hunting season is scheduled to begin later that year in October.Hunters who receive permits will be allowed to hunt in areas within the state's designated elk zone where elk are present."They'll be able to basically hunt any area in the elk zone that has elk; it'll be private land as well as game lands," McVey said.However, anyone planning to hunt on private property must first obtain permission from the landowner.Wildlife officials also said hunters must follow all state hunting regulations. Anyone found violating the rules could face fines or other legal penalties.In addition, every elk harvested during the season must be reported to the NCWRC and presented to the agency as required under the new law.
Article Summary: Elk were once found across much of North Carolina but disappeared from the state many years ago because of overhunting and habitat loss. Wildlife agencies later began efforts to bring them back to western North Carolina, and the animals have slowly established a stable population over the past 25 years.

Article Title: Archaeologists uncover rare 2,000-year-old Liubo game boards in Han Dynasty tombs, but its rules remain one of history's greatest mysteries
Article Text:
Image: AI Generated

Rare Liubo game boards discovered inside Han Dynasty tombs

What was Liubo, and why are its rules still unknown

Archaeology suggests Liubo was played at banquets as well as in tombs

Why Liubo remains one of archaeology's greatest unsolved puzzles

Centuries before chess spread across Asia, another board game captivated people throughout ancient China. Known as Liubo, it was played by emperors, nobles and ordinary families during the Han Dynasty, appearing so frequently that complete game sets were buried alongside the dead. Yet despite its popularity more than 2,000 years ago, the game's rules have almost entirely vanished. A recent archaeological discovery of rare Liubo game boards carved into Han Dynasty tombs has renewed interest in one of China's greatest historical mysteries. The find not only highlights the game's importance in everyday life and burial traditions but also underscores a remarkable paradox: archaeologists know what the board looked like, what pieces players used and where the game was played, yet no one can say with certainty how a match actually unfolded.Archaeologists identified two Liubo boards engraved directly onto square bricks inside Han Dynasty tombs dating to around 2,000 years ago. The discovery formed part of a larger excavation that also revealed pottery figurines, ceramic vessels and other funerary objects.Although Liubo boards have been discovered before, archaeologists rarely find them preserved in their original burial context. Their placement inside tombs suggests the game held lasting significance beyond recreation.During the Han Dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE), objects interred with the deceased often reflected activities or possessions considered valuable in the afterlife.Evidence from the Metropolitan Museum of Art supports this interpretation. Its well-preserved Liubo Board and Pieces, dating from the 1st century BCE–1st century CE, includes gaming pieces made from earthenware and bone. The museum notes that Liubo was "a popular game in the Han dynasty" and that such sets embodied wishes for the continuation of life after death.Liubo emerged no later than the Warring States period and remained one of China's most widely played board games for several centuries before gradually disappearing after the Han Dynasty.Players competed on a square board decorated with a distinctive TLV pattern, using gaming pieces and throwing six casting sticks or, in some versions, dice, to determine movement. Beyond these basic elements, certainty quickly disappears.In his influential study, ‘ A Tricky Game: A Re-evaluation of Liubo Based on Archaeological and Textual Evidence ,’ Dr Armin Selbitschka of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich argues that modern scholarship has often overstated the game's supposed mystical or divinatory nature. After examining archaeological discoveries alongside surviving historical texts, he concludes that Liubo was primarily a game of entertainment, even though symbolic and religious associations emerged in certain regions during the later Eastern Han period.Crucially, no ancient instruction manual explaining the rules has survived. Historians have proposed several reconstructions based on excavated boards, gaming pieces and literary references, but none has achieved scholarly consensus. As a result, Liubo remains one of the few major ancient board games whose equipment is well documented while its gameplay remains largely unknown.The new discovery fits a broader archaeological pattern seen across Han Dynasty China. Selbitschka's research examined dozens of excavated tombs containing Liubo equipment and found that game boards frequently appeared alongside food vessels, drinking cups, musical instruments and figurines. Rather than representing isolated ritual objects, these groupings resemble scenes of banquets and social gatherings recreated inside tombs.The study argues that Liubo occupied an important place in elite entertainment. Historical writings by authors such as Sima Qian also refer to the game in descriptions of court life, competitions and leisure, reinforcing archaeological evidence that it was a familiar pastime rather than an obscure ceremonial practice.This interpretation contrasts with older theories that viewed Liubo mainly as a tool for divination because of the board's distinctive TLV design. According to Selbitschka, archaeological evidence indicates that recreational play remained its principal role throughout most of the Western Han period.Few ancient games present such an unusual challenge to historians. Archaeologists have uncovered exquisitely crafted lacquered boards, ceramic playing pieces, bronze fittings, carved stone examples and complete Liubo sets from royal mausoleums, aristocratic burials and Han Dynasty tombs across China. Museums, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art, preserve these remarkable artefacts. Paintings, stone reliefs and funerary objects even depict people gathered around Liubo boards, confirming that it was far more than an obscure pastime.A carved board inside a Han Dynasty tomb or a complete gaming set recovered from an ancient burial may appear modest compared with spectacular treasures of gold or jade, yet each provides another clue about a game that dominated Chinese society for centuries before disappearing almost completely by the end of the Tang Dynasty. Future excavations may eventually uncover an illustrated manual, an inscribed game board or a more detailed written account capable of solving the mystery.Until then, Liubo remains one of archaeology's most intriguing unsolved puzzles. It is a rare example of a game whose equipment, artwork and cultural significance have survived for more than two millennia, while the knowledge required to play it has quietly slipped out of history.
Article Summary: Rare Liubo game boards discovered inside Han Dynasty tombs. Archaeologists identified two Liubos engraved directly onto square bricks. The discovery formed part of a larger excavation that also revealed pottery figurines, ceramic vessels and other funerary objects. The find highlights the game's importance in everyday life.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: IPL craze costs techie Rs 1.46 lakh in fake RCB vs CSK ticket scam
Article Text:
Image credit: AI generated pic

RCB register their second win

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the demand for IPL tickets is too high every season? Yes, it's excessive. No, it's just right. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: IPL comes and the demand for tickets and passes go soaring up by the fans. The desperation to get inside the stadium to watch their favourite teams in action in the IPL go high and high. When the tickets get sold out, the demand gets too hig, and the cricket fans even ask for tickets in black. But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) beat Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday. Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal put on a marauding batting show to lift RCB to a daunting 250/3. RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Cops save 6-yr-old after years of torture by mentally ill mother
Article Text:
New Delhi:





A six-year-old girl who was routinely neglected, abused and forced into domestic labour by her mentally ill mother in GTB Enclave was rescued following police intervention earlier this month.For two years, residents at Janta Flats reported hearing frequent disturbances from the house, where the mother, a former schoolteacher with untreated psychiatric issues, denied her daughter proper meals, forced her to perform household chores, and locked her outside naked.Early attempts to step in failed due to the woman’s threats of self-harm, prompting local police to tread safely and wait for the right opportunity.DCP (Shahdara) Rajendra Prasad Meena formed a team under Inspector Brijesh Mishra, SHO of GTB Enclave police station. Police conducted a two-month reconnaissance of the area to verify the allegations. Cops visited the family many times, but the child appeared withdrawn and did not speak ill of her mother, possibly out of fear.A senior police officer said, “Neighbours flooded us with calls and complaints describing continuous verbal abuse that echoed through the building.They reported that the woman routinely threw household pots and cookware out of the flat in fits of rage, often locking her daughter outside completely naked as punishment. At other times, she would leave the apartment altogether, locking the girl inside to fend for herself alone in the dark. ”At odd hours in the night, the child would be screamed at, denied basic meals and made to scrub floors and handle chores far beyond her age.Earlier this month, a neighbour managed to record a video of the abuse. “It showed the girl, completely unclothed and visibly malnourished, standing in front of the neighbours while her mother berated her,” the officer said. Armed with this evidence, the GTB Enclave SHO immediately asked Child Welfare Committee (CWC) to intervene.A rescue team, led by two women police officers and CWC officials, entered the unsanitary flat and rescued the girl, who was found in an extremely weak and fragile state after months of deprivation.While the child was sent to CWC for medical evaluation and trauma care, the officers arranged for the mother’s transfer to IHBAS for formal psychiatric treatment. Police are now working to enrol the child in a school while taking regular follow-up of the woman’s health.
Article Summary: A six-year-old girl was routinely neglected, abused and forced into domestic labour by her mentally ill mother in GTB Enclave. For two years, residents at Janta Flats reported hearing frequent disturbances from the house. The mother, a former schoolteacher with untreated psychiatric issues, denied her daughter proper meals and forced her to perform household chores.

Article Title: Deshbhakt defeated andhbhakt, it’s now BJP vs Bharat: Thackerays
Article Text:
The victory rally at Shivaji Park turned into a high-octane political platform

Mumbai:

Deshbhakt

andhbhakt

khadda





A massive student-led victory gathering on Sunday turned into a high-octane political platform as the Thackeray cousins mounted a sharp attack on the Centre.MNS chief Raj Thackeray led a one-minute silence in memory of the 21 students who died by suicide following the NEET paper leak controversy, praising the youth for taking the fight directly to the establishment.Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray framed the gathering as the start of a broader democratic movement. “All of you came here together, having forgotten religion, caste and creed, and this wave of yours has today made the rulers silent. This is the true avatar of Vishnu,” he said. “No election has been won today.(patriots) have defeated(blind followers). This is the beginning of a bigger struggle. This is a fight between BJP and India,” he asserted.Training his guns on PM Narendra Modi , Uddhav urged a shift from partisan politics to governance. “Your ministers are busy breaking political parties. Tell them to start working for the nation,” he said. “How painful was it to remove your favourite Dharmendra [Pradhan, former Union education minister] from the cabinet? Was that pain greater than what families suffered when their children took their own lives? Today isn’t the day for long speeches—deeds are more important than words, and this protest of yours will be written in golden words in the democratic history of this country.Uddhav then criticised the wider cabinet, alleging that finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman ignored the falling rupee and the rising inflation and instead explained the “benefits” of a paper leak, while “defence minister Rajnath Singh should be protecting borders but is defending Pradhan”.Directing the final jibe at transport minister Nitin Gadkari, Uddhav called him the(potholes) minister for pushing E20 fuel and warned, “This is definitely the next issue.”Urging the crowd to sustain the momentum, he said: “Do not let this awakening fade away. You have shown the strength of the people.”
Article Summary: MNS chief Raj Thackeray led a one-minute silence in memory of the 21 students who died by suicide following the NEET paper leak controversy. “No election has been won today.(patriots) have defeated(blind followers). This is the beginning of a bigger struggle. This is a fight between BJP and India,” he asserted.

Article Title: Pen cap stuck in 10-year-old Mumbai girl’s lung for 7 years; doctors misdiagnose her with TB, asthma
Article Text:
Initially misdiagnosed with tuberculosis and asthma, she received improper treatment until a CT scan exposed the collapsed lung (Representative image)





MUMBAI: A 10-year-old girl required part of her lung to be removed after a pen cap remained lodged near her left lower lobe bronchus for over seven years, as multiple doctors misdiagnosed her abnormal X-ray as tuberculosis or asthma.Speaking to TOI, the girl’s mother, Dharavi resident Maimuna Shaikh, said that when symptoms like a persistent cough and sudden weight loss appeared, several clinicians treated her for suspected infectious diseases and prescribed antibiotics.She was then referred to a BMC hospital, where doctors put her on presumptive TB treatment even though her sputum sample was negative.A resident doctor, who was with the hospital then and was partly involved in Mysha’s case, said this was likely one of the rare instances where an exact diagnosis was very difficult to establish given the location of the object, and treatment was provided based on clinical presentation.“We cannot just give out the Anti-Koch’s Therapy (AKT) regimen unless there is a strong indication. The treatment even with a negative result is useful for future doctors to rule out TB,” the doctor said.Even after the TB treatment, when Maimuna saw her child not getting any better, she took her to another private hospital, where doctors told the family Mysha had asthma and prescribed an inhaler for relief.Dr Indu Khosla, a pulmonologist at SRCC Children’s Hospital (Narayana Health) who was involved in the case, said that most doctors saw pneumonia that would not resolve and prescribed anti-TB medicines.“Further investigations for a foreign body inside the lung should have been suspected, but these are differences of opinion, and doctors cannot be blamed for it,” she said.She added that a CT scan showed a collapsed lung, and because the rest of the organ appeared normal, she suspected an external foreign body.“On the bronchoscopy, we saw a pen cap deeply embedded, we had to involve our ENT team and use more anaesthesia to be able to pull it out,” Dr Khosla said.As soon as it was removed, Mysha felt much better.“About two to three weeks after the procedure, her pneumonia, which involved the left lower lobe and the middle lobe, had reduced and was confined only to the lower lobe. The part of the lung that was not degenerated opened up,” Dr Khosla said.Doctors waited for a month to check if the rest of the affected lung would re-expand, but it did not.Because of heavy infection and irreversible tissue damage, they ultimately had to remove roughly one-third of her lung.Mysha is expected to live a normal life, but Maimuna said she almost lost her daughter to one clinical miss.“We have lost count of expenses so far,” she said.
Article Summary: A 10-year-old girl required part of her lung to be removed after a pen cap remained lodged near her left lower lobe bronchus for over seven years. Multiple doctors misdiagnosed her abnormal X-ray as tuberculosis or asthma. She received improper treatment until a CT scan exposed the collapsed lung.

Article Title: Drunk driver reverses SUV at high speed to avoid check in Mumbai, leaves cop with 15 stitches
Article Text:
The reversing SUV hit constable Ashok Borude’s bike while evading the check on Linking Road





MUMBAI: A 27-year-old executive with a private firm allegedly reversed his SUV at high speed to evade a drink-and-drive check on Linking Road in Khar (W) and crashed into a police patrol bike, injuring a constable, in the early hours of Friday.A breathalyzer test on the driver, Chandivli resident Siddharth Mahalingam (27), found the alcohol level at 166.8 mg/100ml, sources said; the legal blood alcohol concentration limit for driving in India is 30mg/100ml of blood.Khar police arrested Mahalingam and slapped him with non -bailable offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Motor Vehicles Act . Mahalingam was driving back home after a party when the incident took place.The accident left constable Ashok Borude (44) of Khar police station with 12 stitches on his lower jaw and three on his forehead. Borude’s jaw got stuck in the rear glass of the SUV due to the impact of the crash, police said.Bandra traffic police had set up a nakabandi in front of Rajkumar Jewellers to take action against those driving under the influence of alcohol.On Sunday, Borude told TOI: “I was proceeding towards Santacruz for patrol duty around 2 am, when I noticed the black SUV reversing at high speed.I could not move the 220 cc department bike, which I stopped about 25 m away, and the SUV crashed into me. Despite wearing a helmet, my lower jaw got stuck inside the SUV’s rear glass and I got injured due to glass shrads. Luckily, I did not get hit by other vehicles that came from behind. ”Borude, a Kalyan resident, was discharged from hospital after receiving medical assistance and has been advised 10 days’ rest.The police team on checkpoint duty said it was the first time they saw a motorist attempt to flee by driving in reverse at speed despite vehicles approaching from the same direction.Police have booked Mahalingam under BNS sections 110 (attempt to culpable homicide), 125(a) (rash or negligent act that endangers human life or the personal safety of others), 281 (rash or negligent driving or riding on a public way in a manner that endangers human life or is likely to cause hurt or injury), 324(4) (mischief), and under the MV Act sections 184 (dangerous driving) and 185 (driving by a drunk person).Police said the incident occurred barely 11 days after an eight-year-old girl, Reva Pawar, 8, was knocked down in Andheri (W) by a speeding scooterist riding in the wrong direction on July 15.Amboli police arrested the accused, scrap-seller Shabir Yusuf Shaikh, 30, from Ajmer Junction railway station on July 19 and invoked an additional charge of attempt to commit culpable homicide.Reva is undergoing treatment at Cooper Hospital for a skull fracture, and has been advised two months’ complete bed rest.
Article Summary: Siddharth Mahalingam, 27, allegedly reversed his SUV at high speed to evade a drink-and-drive check on Linking Road in Khar (W) and crashed into a police patrol bike. The accident left constable Ashok Borude (44) of Khar police station with 12 stitches on his lower jaw and three on his forehead. Borude’s jaw got stuck in the rear glass of the SUV due to the impact.

Article Title: ‘I will hug him tightly and perform an aarti’: Abhijeet Dipke’s parents express relief after weeks of anxiety
Article Text:
Parents expressed immense joy and relief following the successful campaign by Abhijeet Dipke.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Relief and celebration replaced months of anxiety for the parents of the Cockroach Janata Party ( CJP ) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday after the campaign spearheaded by him culminated in Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation."I will ask him to come home early. If he does not come, we will go and bring him back. I will hug him tightly and perform an aarti for him. The last time he was here, he did not allow me to do that, saying he was not some prominent person," said Abhijeet's mother, Anita Dipke, struggling to hold back her tears."I am extremely happy. His honesty has won. The support of the youth helped him, and he achieved a big victory," she said.Anita said she had remained anxious ever since her son returned to India and launched the agitation seeking Union education minister Pradhan's resignation over the NEET paper leak issue.She said she lost sleep after the CJP began its protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, news agency PTI reported."I was worried all the time. I had sleepless nights. Every morning, I was scared to even look at my phone, fearing I would see a disturbing video.I would immediately call his friends to ask if he was safe," Anita said.She said Abhijeet's friends repeatedly assured her that he would become emotional whenever he came to know about her worries and that they were always with him, taking care of him.Remembering the day the agitation began, Anita said she had cried out of fear and helplessness. "Today, the tears in my eyes are of happiness," she said.Calling Pradhan's resignation a "victory of the youth", Anita said thousands of youngsters had worked relentlessly to make the campaign successful.She, however, said she did not think her son would launch a political party and believed he would continue working in the social sector, PTI reported.Abhijeet's father, Bhagwanrao Dipke, said the family had been living in constant fear since his son floated the CJP despite having no political background."We were all worried when he took the political plunge. He went against my wishes. Nobody in our family had any political background," he said.The family had even appealed to Abhijeet not to return to India from the United States in June as they feared he could be arrested."We were so scared that during the initial days we left home and stayed in Konkan. We were under tremendous pressure. There were threats of physical harm to us," Bhagwanrao said.He said the stress had taken a severe toll on the family's health."We became so weak that we could barely stand. We were eating barely one roti a day. We could neither eat properly nor sleep. He was attacked twice during the agitation," Bhagwanrao said.Recalling the events of July 20, Bhagwanrao said seeing a police officer pull down Abhijeet's microphone reminded him of a battle scene from the film "Border"."I felt that if my Abhijeet fell into the hands of the police, he would not survive. By God's grace, he is safe. I honestly feel he should now come home and stay with us," he said.On Pradhan's resignation, Bhagwanrao said the Union minister had displayed "a big heart" by stepping down while asking students to concentrate on their education."This should not be seen as anybody's victory or defeat. Leaving such a high post requires a big heart. Even while resigning, he thought about the interests of students," he said.Describing his son as a well-educated person who had carefully planned the agitation before launching it, Bhagwanrao said he was uncertain about Abhijeet's next political move."He had earlier worked with (AAP leader) Arvind Kejriwal and has seen politics closely. I personally do not like politics, so I have no idea what he will do next. But I will be with him," Bhagwanrao said.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Parents of CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke expressed joy and relief following the successful campaign by him. The campaign spearheaded by him culminated in Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. His mother, Anita Dipke, said she had remained anxious ever since her son returned to India.

Article Title: Satisfied with current tasks, says CM Devendra Fadnavis; won’t let him shift to Delhi: Wife Amruta Fadnavis
Article Text:
Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, his wife Amruta Fadnavis (File Photo)

ji





KOLHAPUR: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday brushed aside speculation about a possible induction into the Union cabinet, saying he was “satisfied” with his current responsibilities. His wife, Amruta Fadnavis , said she would not allow him to shift to New Delhi.The remarks came after the couple performed the official Mahapuja of Lord Vitthal and Goddess Rukmini at the Vitthal-Rukhmini temple on the occasion of Ashadhi Ekadashi. Later in the evening, Fadnavis left for New Delhi.More than 20 lakh warkari devotees thronged the temple town for the annual pilgrimage.This was the sixth time Devendra and Amruta Fadnavis performed the Ashadhi Ekadashi Mahapuja. Fadnavis had also attended the Kartiki Ekadashi Mahapuja twice while serving as deputy chief minister.When asked whether they would return next year to perform the ritual, Amruta initially said they would do so whether they are in Mumbai, Nagpur or Pandharpur. However, when specifically asked about speculation that Fadnavis may soon be moved to Delhi, she said, “I will also not let Devendramove to Delhi.”The comment came amid fresh political chatter after Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut said that Fadnavis could be considered for a role in the Union cabinet.“I feel that Devendra Fadnavis could replace Dharmendra Pradhan. He is a lawyer, he is educated and presents different subjects well. There has been discussion about Fadnavis going to Delhi and he could get the opportunity now,” Raut said.Speaking on the ongoing students’ agitation, Amruta Fadnavis said demonstrations were justified as long as they remained focused on the issue of examination paper leaks.“It was absolutely OK if the agitation had been restricted to the paper leak. Govt has been taking corrective measures in the background, and now we are seeing the results too,” she said.Chief minister Fadnavis said there were two distinct strands within the agitation, one comprising students genuinely concerned about their future and another attempting to exploit the issue politically.“Considering this situation, Sonam Wangchuk broke his fast; all his demands were accepted, and he also appealed to everyone to go ahead peacefully,” he said.Asked about the protest called by the Thackeray cousins in Mumbai on Sunday, Fadnavis said political motives appeared to be driving the mobilisation.“Everyone has the right in a democracy to speak their opinion. But I feel there is less possibility of this protest having any relation with the students. There is a greater possibility of efforts to establish themselves (the Thackerays) in politics again. Still our well-wishers are with them,” he said.Fadnavis also participated in the traditional Ashadhi Ekadashi celebrations, praying for the welfare of the state, good rainfall and prosperity for farmers as lakhs of devotees converged on Pandharpur for one of Maharashtra’s largest religious gatherings.
Article Summary: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis says he is'satisfied' with his current responsibilities. His wife, Amruta, said she would not allow him to shift to New Delhi. The remarks came after the couple performed the official Mahapuja at the Vitthal-Rukhmini temple.
